events.type: sector move (macro: bond yields and oil)
events.summary: Chip stocks fell from the open on Thursday as long-term Treasury yields and oil rose. At 10:05 ET, AMD traded at $632.96 (down 2%) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) at $572.20 (down 2%); 24/7 Wall St. wrote: 'Rising Treasury yields and surging oil prices are hammering chip stocks.' At the close the 10-year Treasury yield was 5.233%, 'near levels not seen since 2007', and oil was up about 3% to near $91 a barrel amid Middle East tensions (Schwab Network). Yahoo's live blog put Brent near $104 and WTI near $91.
events.why_it_matters: Higher interest rates make far-off profits worth less today, which hits fast-growing, highly valued stocks like AMD hardest; the selloff began before the OpenAI story, so it had at least two causes.

events.type: customer/industry news (largest AI customer's revenue questioned)
events.summary: The Financial Times reported, from financial documents, that OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was 'approaching $50 billion at the end of September', about $20 billion below the roughly $70 billion widely reported late in September. The FT says the gap came from investors adjusting OpenAI's figure to match Anthropic's method (which counts full sales through cloud partners) and then adding OpenAI's reported 70%+ growth, so it reflects how the figure was calculated, not $20 billion of lost sales. AI stocks fell: Oracle -5.5%, CoreWeave nearly -8%, Nvidia almost -3%, Broadcom -4.35%, AMD 'around 4%' (Euronews). AMD closed at $620.68 (-3.90%, data/prices); the Nasdaq-100 fell 1.39% and the S&P 500 0.47% (Schwab Network). Yahoo's live blog said the semiconductor index 'declined as much as 4% before trimming gains'. OpenAI had not commented as of Friday (Euronews). Exact publication time of the FT story: not available (Yahoo's write-up posted 13:40 ET).
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI is one of AMD's anchor customers: a 6-gigawatt, multi-year GPU agreement that AMD said would bring 'tens of billions of dollars in revenue' (AMD, 2025-10-06). Smaller OpenAI revenue raises the question of how it pays for its chip commitments. Nothing in the report says OpenAI changed its AMD order.

events.type: background: filing facts re-read (warrants and Helios business model)
events.summary: Not new news (10-Q filed August 2026), but new to the news log and relevant to the thesis. (1) The 10-Q says AMD issued warrants to OpenAI (October 2025) and Meta (February 2026), each for 'up to 160 million shares' at $0.01, vesting with GPU purchase milestones and AMD share-price targets; 'As of June 27, 2026, no warrant tranches had vested'. Up to 320 million shares against 1,632,475,042 outstanding on 2026-07-29 is about 19.6% more shares, or about 16.4% of the enlarged total (researcher's calculation; the Motley Fool piece of 2026-10-05 says about 16%). (2) Meta also has a multi-year agreement to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, first gigawatt on MI450. (3) On Helios the 10-Q says AMD 'develop[s] and license[s]' the rack design 'for implementation by customers and their manufacturing partners', expected to start shipping in the second half of fiscal 2026, and 'Although we supply certain products used in Helios-based system, we do not manufacture or sell the completed Helios rack systems.'
events.why_it_matters: Pillar 5 counts World Labs dilution (about 0.8%) but not these warrants, which could add far more shares if the deals succeed. Thesis 2 talks about AMD 'selling complete AI server racks'; the 10-Q says AMD sells the chips and other parts inside them and licenses the design, not the finished rack. Whether the thesis wording should change is for the main session to propose, not decide.

products.name: OpenAI 6-gigawatt agreement (AMD Instinct MI450 series GPUs and later generations)
products.what_it_is: A multi-year, multi-generation agreement under which OpenAI deploys 6 gigawatts of AMD data-center GPUs, starting with 1 gigawatt of Instinct MI450 in the second half of 2026.
products.analogy: Like an airline ordering a large fleet from a planemaker over several years: delivered in batches, paid as planes arrive, and the airline also gets an option to own part of the planemaker.
products.buyers: OpenAI (and, under a similar 6 GW agreement from February 2026, Meta).
products.how_it_works: AMD sells GPUs (chips that do huge numbers of calculations at once, which AI needs), built into rack systems in OpenAI's data centers. 'Gigawatts' measures the power the installed chips use, a way to size very large orders. AMD gave OpenAI a warrant (the right to buy shares) for up to 160 million AMD shares at $0.01, vesting only as purchase milestones and AMD share-price targets are met.
products.sales: Not disclosed per customer. AMD said the partnership 'is expected to deliver tens of billions of dollars in revenue for AMD' and to be 'highly accretive' to non-GAAP EPS (2025-10-06). As of 2026-06-27 no warrant tranche had vested, so the first purchase milestone had not been reached by then (10-Q). Proxy: data-center segment revenue $6.7bn in Q2 2026, +107% (AMD Q2 2026 results).
products.stage: Announced; first 1 GW deployment of MI450 scheduled to start in 2H 2026. Shipments to OpenAI not yet confirmed in any source read.
products.size_for_company: 'Tens of billions' of dollars over several years, against total revenue of $11.54bn in Q2 2026 (one quarter). Annual amount not disclosed.
products.competition: NVIDIA's GPU systems (OpenAI's main supplier); custom chips OpenAI is developing with Broadcom (background, not re-verified this run).
products.why_investors_care: It is the first proof that a top AI lab will buy AMD at scale. Thursday's FT report on OpenAI's revenue is why the market questioned it this week.
products.watch_next: Lisa Su's OCP keynote on 2026-10-12 and the Q3 call on 2026-11-03: any confirmation that MI450 shipments to OpenAI have begun, any vesting of the first warrant tranche, and any change in OpenAI's commitment.

products.name: Helios rack-scale platform
products.what_it_is: AMD's design for a complete AI server cabinet (rack) combining Instinct MI450-series GPUs, EPYC CPUs and networking, built by customers and their manufacturing partners.
products.analogy: Like a reference kitchen design from an appliance maker: the maker sells the ovens and fridges and publishes the blueprint, while a contractor builds and installs the kitchen.
products.buyers: Named customers for MI450/Helios include OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic (Anthropic: up to 2 GW in Helios racks, first gigawatt from H1 2027).
products.how_it_works: Per the 10-Q, AMD 'develop[s] and license[s]' Helios 'for implementation by customers and their manufacturing partners'. It supplies 'certain products used in Helios-based system' but does 'not manufacture or sell the completed Helios rack systems.'
products.sales: Not disclosed. Proxy: data-center segment revenue $6.7bn in Q2 2026 (+107%), which will include AMD's chips sold into Helios systems.
products.stage: Expected to start shipping in the second half of fiscal 2026 (10-Q). A tier-3 conference write-up says shipments begin in Q3 2026 and ramp in Q4; not verified against a primary source.
products.size_for_company: Not disclosed; the large GPU agreements (OpenAI 6 GW, Meta 6 GW, Anthropic up to 2 GW) are built around it.
products.why_investors_care: Thesis 2 relies on Helios raising the value per customer. Because AMD sells the parts and licenses the design, the gain shows up in how much AMD silicon goes into each rack, not in sales of finished racks.
products.watch_next: OCP Global Summit keynote 2026-10-12 (4:15 p.m. PT): first-shipment confirmation or any timing change. Q3 call 2026-11-03.
